candidates.title: Unreproducible mode has two sources of truth: write_reg(iunrep) changes the hashed register while every path reads the config copy, and store then writes a directory that refuses to load
candidates.component: Machine API (write_reg, store/load) and the host-side checks of the unreproducible mode (machine::is_unreproducible) used by run/collect/log/uarch/store
candidates.role: Honest operator for store/load and the collectors (AUDIT.md component table: storing, loading, collect_*). write_reg itself is in 'the rest of the machine API', where a production node would not normally write iunrep, so it plays the honest-operator role only if a node calls it on its path. Both ratings are given below.
candidates.location: src/machine.hpp:857-859 (is_unreproducible reads m_c.processor.registers.iunrep, the config); src/machine.cpp:1444-1445 (write_reg case reg::iunrep writes the shadow register without restriction, unlike mvendorid/marchid/mimpid, which throw 'register is read-only'); src/machine.cpp:222-224 (validate_processor_shadow: shadow iunrep must equal config iunrep, checked only at create/load); src/machine.cpp:426-431 and 487 (store refuses only when the config says unreproducible, then writes the stale config next to the shadow-state file); every check 'cannot collect hashes from unreproducible machines' / 'microarchitecture cannot be used with unreproducible machines' (machine.cpp:2194, 2245, 2445, 2619, 2770) and poll_external_interrupts (2348) read the config copy.
candidates.description: THREAT_MODEL section 2 lists 'the unreproducible mode' as part of the hashed state, and R14 says 'The unreproducible mode is fixed at creation and recorded in the hashed state'. The manual (doc/README.md around line 7381) calls iunrep 'a creation-time mode'. But the emulator keeps two copies: the hashed shadow register iunrep and the config field m_c.processor.registers.iunrep. They are compared only when a machine is created or loaded. machine::write_reg accepts reg::iunrep and changes only the hashed copy. Every behavior that depends on the mode reads only the config copy: the refusal of collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, log_step_uarch, run_uarch and store, and host interrupt polling and time advance in WFI (poll_external_interrupts). After write_reg('iunrep', 1) on a reproducible machine, the hash commits to an unreproducible machine, but the machine still collects, logs, runs the uarch and stores. The stored directory keeps config iunrep=0 and shadow iunrep=1, so loading it throws 'iunrep mismatch between shadow state and config'. After write_reg('iunrep', 0) on an unreproducible machine, the hash commits to a reproducible machine while host VirtIO devices and wall-clock WFI stay active. So the hashed register R14 relies on does not determine the behavior. That violates R2: 'Every register and every configuration value that affects a transition has one source of truth in the hashed state, and every path reads it from there.'
candidates.trigger: A trusted machine-API caller (C, Lua or JSON-RPC) calls write_reg('iunrep', v) with v different from the creation value, then runs, collects, stores or loads. No guest can trigger it, because R8 keeps the guest away from iunrep, and machine::write_word refuses writes from the guest to unknown shadow words. No input or log can trigger it either.
candidates.reachability: Not reachable by an adversary. It needs a trusted caller to write iunrep through the machine API. Neither the PRT player in doc/recipes nor any honest-operator flow writes iunrep. The state it produces (hashed iunrep different from the config) cannot come from any input sequence on a valid template, because only write_reg changes iunrep.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The section 8 exclusion covers 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented (section 4)'. Whether this write is 'as documented' is the deciding fact. The manual calls iunrep 'a creation-time mode', R14 says it is 'fixed at creation', and the emulator already treats the other identity registers (mvendorid/marchid/mimpid) as read-only. On that reading the API does not perform the write as documented, and the finding is not excluded. On the opposite reading (write_reg may write any register), it is out of scope. 2. Role: the store/load and collector checks are honest-operator components (AUDIT.md table). write_reg is 'the rest of the machine API', honest operator only where a production node plausibly calls it, which it does not here. So the operation that triggers it is off the honest operator's path. 3. High/Medium cases: Medium, 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)'. store writes a directory whose config contradicts its hashed contents, and the directory then fails to load. It also matches 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'. If the manual is right that the mode is creation-time, the API should refuse the write. 4. Critical: no. It does not happen at a reachable state or on the honest operator's path. 5. Otherwise Low: 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'. Claimed: Medium if write_reg(iunrep) counts as used as documented, Low if it counts as misuse, Out of scope if the manual allows writing iunrep.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (alternatively Low; out of scope if writing iunrep is documented as allowed)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not break the section 1 goal directly, because no adversary can reach it. It still violates R2 (one source of truth in the hashed state) and weakens R14: a reproducible-looking hash no longer guarantees that host polling and VirtIO are off, and the reverse. A tool or operator that changes the register, for example to 'normalize' a template, would create a stored machine that later fails to load, which is a completeness hazard if such a directory were ever the guaranteed snapshot.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R2/iunrep.lua against the in-tree build. It uses the baremetal-minimal config. On a reproducible machine, write_reg('iunrep',1) succeeds and read_reg returns 1. log_step_uarch is still allowed. store succeeds. cartesi.machine(dir) then fails with 'iunrep mismatch between shadow state and config'. On a machine created with iunrep=1, write_reg('iunrep',0) succeeds and collect_mcycle_root_hashes still refuses with 'cannot collect hashes from unreproducible machines', so the behavior follows the config, not the hashed register.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: create a machine from the baremetal-minimal config and call write_reg('iunrep', 1). Required behavior: either write_reg raises 'register is read-only', as it does for marchid, or the machine's behavior and the stored directory follow the hashed value (store, then load the directory, succeeds and the loaded machine refuses log_step_uarch). Exit 1 if write_reg succeeds and load of the stored directory fails, or if is_unreproducible-guarded operations disagree with read_reg('iunrep').

not_covered: Full differential test of native run vs uarch vs collect_* on Linux workloads with timer interrupts at arbitrary stop/resume points. Reasoned only: interrupts are raised whenever the outer loop runs, and the uarch enters the outer loop every mcycle, so agreement relies on the invariant that no pending-and-enabled interrupt survives an inner-loop iteration. Every mip/mie/mideleg/mstatus/sip/CLINT/PLIC writer I inspected returns success_and_serve_interrupts, but I did not test it exhaustively. assert_no_brk explicitly tolerates pending M-level interrupts in S/U mode. That is benign only if the invariant holds.

Off-chain verifiers through JSON-RPC and the encoding of prt-ethereum.lua append_log, beyond the rejection step+reset case I ran. Checked: step+reset at the rejecting mcycle agrees between collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, verify_step_uarch+verify_reset_uarch and the regenerated Solidity stepThenReset on the EVM harness. The send_cmio_response no-op branches (oversized input, non-accepted yield) were not run on the EVM.

Copying and persistence paths (clone_stored, sync_stored, SHARING_ALL load/destroy, fork_server/swap/rebind) under write-TLB dirty marks and cached hash-tree data. Only reviewed the code (destructor and replace_memory_range mark write-TLB pages). This belongs mostly to the R9/O1/O2 angles.

collect_mcycle_root_hashes / collect_mcycle_bundle with console output to_buffer and with automatic yields landing exactly on sampling points and bundle ends (final_bundle_sibling_hashes bookkeeping). Reviewed, not run.

Dave referee-model geometry: I checked that log2step [38,0], height [54,38], CartesiStateTransition's counter-to-form map, Commitment.toCycle and DaveConsensus input Merkle roots match the emulator (24/48/20, imcyclemax = delivery mcycle + 2^48 - 1, writeLengthLog2Size vs ceilLog2). I did not audit match/A1/A2/A5 logic, clocks or epoch sealing, the input-limit cap included.

The worst-case number of uarch cycles per main-processor instruction under adversarial guests. A spot check found sfence.vma about 17.6k, fsqrt.d/fdiv.d on subnormals about 3-4k, and mret with a TLB flush about 17.6k, all far below 2^20 - 1. Combined trap, flush and page-walk sequences were not searched exhaustively.
mcycle-level log_step/verify_step (ZK step log): only checked that the replay uses the revert hash on rejection. Out of scope (ZK).
